page: Amazon Web Services m8g.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by 32 physical cores based on the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture operating at 2.8 GHz, each core runs a single thread, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs. The processor cache architecture integrates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. System memory measures 128 GB, reflecting a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. This configuration includes no integrated local storage and features no discrete GPU accelerators, while network connectivity operates at a baseline speed of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across multi-core and memory-heavy metrics. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 21608 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 397.95 GB/sec alongside 191.37 GB/sec write bandwidth. Strong throughput is also seen in database and caching operations, with 67.6 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark database score of 46696.21, and static web throughput of 72.62 GB/sec. By contrast, single-thread execution falls within average ranges, illustrated by a single-core Geekbench score of 1863, and large-parameter language model prompt processing scores within the lower tiers.

The instance provides high resource density for horizontal scaling, distributed caching layers, relational databases, Clang software build farms, and multi-threaded enterprise services. Workloads dependent on local ephemeral disks must rely on network-attached alternatives, and applications constrained by single-threaded performance or hardware acceleration will not fully leverage this architecture.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, utilizing 32 dedicated physical cores on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 silicon running at 2.8 GHz. Paired with 128 GB of memory, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 36 MB L3 cache and a 15 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 21608 and 397.95 GB/sec uncached read throughput. It exhibits strong operational density for data stores, generating 46696.21 points in PassMark database tests and 67.6 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread benchmarks and large LLM prompt processing remain at median or lower percentiles, the instance effectively supports multi-threaded microservices, web serving clusters, in-memory caching systems, and compilation pipelines.
